title: the retired-grammar sweep MUST NOT reinterpret ordinary TypeScript: `try`/`catch`/`orelse` as property names, `catch` as a class member, and `!` as negation all stay ordinary code
notes: specification/compatibility.mdx, 'Source Relationship': 'Shared syntax MUST retain TypeScript behavior unless the Smithers specification explicitly assigns different semantics.' specification/control-flow.mdx, 'Existing TypeScript Forms': 'Adding expression forms MUST NOT reinterpret an existing TypeScript statement in a way that changes observable behavior.' The nine negative cases in this area pin that each retired form IS rejected; this case pins the other half of the same rule, which is the dangerous direction for a textual migration sweep. poc/src/language/README.md states the intended boundary and names these exact shapes: 'Recognition is a grammar property, not token adjacency ... a word used as a property name is never the operator. `{ try: doThing, catch: handleIt }`, `{ orelse: 7 }`, `class A { catch() {} }`, `Array<uses>`, and `{ ok: !failed }` are ordinary code.' A false positive here makes valid TypeScript unwritable in .sm and would silently rewrite a migrating program.
